title: It’s a Shaolin Thanksgiving! Wu-Tang Clan, Chad Smith Light Up Halftime at Detroit Lions NFL Game
summary: The hip-hop legends hit a nearly seven-minute tag-team medley of greatest hits that was announced as “the wrap-up” of its Wu-Tang Forever: The Final Chamber farewell tour.
content: Wu-Tang Clan created a Shaolin Thanksgiving experience in Detroit on Thursday afternoon (Nov. 26), joined by Red Hot Chili Peppers drummer — and homeboy — Chad Smith for a halftime performance at Ford Field for the Lions’ annual Thanksgiving game. The collective — recently inducted into the Rock And Roll Hall of Fame — lit up the stadium with a nearly seven-minute tag-team medley of greatest hits that was announced as “the wrap-up” of its Wu-Tang Forever: The Final Chamber farewell tour . Flanked by flags bearing the Wu-Tang and Lions logos, and with 500 fan volunteers moshing on the field in front of the stage and on its wings, the nine surviving MCs — plus Young Dirty Bastard in place of his late father Ol’ Dirty Bastard and DJ Mathematics — kicked off with “Triumph,” then rolled through bits of “4th Chamber,” “Da Mystery of Chessboxin’,” “Protect Ya Neck,” “Method Man,” “Shimmy Shimmy Ya,” “Ice Cream” and “C.R.E.A.M.” The RZA-led “Wu-Tang Clan Ain’t Nuthing ta F’ Wit” finished the set with the group members on the field amidst the fans, with smoke jets shooting up from the stage. The Lions cheerleading squad also took part in the show, sporting T-shirts with a glittering Wu-Tang/Lions mash-up logo. “Who’s got it better than me?” Smith — who participated in a 2025 remix of “Wu-Tang Clan Ain’t Nuthing Ta F’ Wit” — enthused to Billboard during rehearsals at the stadium on Wednesday. “This is the…Wu-Tang Clan. It’s the halftime show, the biggest game of the year, and the Lions. I’m in my home town, and I get to play drums at halftime with the legendary Wu-Tang — come on! I’m the queen of the ball. And I love those guys. I mean, as far as iconic ’90s hip-hop goes, there’s Nas, maybe, but I love Wu-Tang.” The Wu-Tang booking was also a personal pleasure for Lions general manager Brad Holmes , an unabashed fanboy who attended the rehearsal as well as the game. “I would put myself in the die-hard category,” said Holmes, who became a Wu-Tang fan while growing up in Tampa, Fla., and even met U-God after “stalking” the troupe at its hotel before a concert there. “Their music, it really just hit my soul. It’s truly art; I didn’t know how much art it really was, and as I’ve gotten older, the more I listen to it, it just gets even better. When they said Wu-Tang Clan on Thanksgiving, I just” (makes gesture of head exploding).

title: 2027 BRIT Awards Trophy Designed by ‘One of Britain’s Greatest Living Artists’: See Photos
summary: The trophy will be presented to winners at the ceremony on Feb. 27 in Manchester.
content: The 2027 BRIT Awards trophy has been designed by former Turner Prize-winning visual artist Dame Rachel Whiteread (Nov. 27). Each year a different designer shapes a distinct creative vision for their trophy, modeled on the image of Britannia, traditionally represented by a female warrior with a shield and helmet. In recent years, the trophy has been designed by iconic names such as Dame Vivienne Westwood, Sir Peter Blake, Tracey Emin, Dame Zaha Hadid, and last year’s designer, Matthew Williamson. Whiteread took on 2027’s assignment, and her trophy will be presented to winners at the ceremony on Feb. 27 at the Co-op Live in Manchester. In 1993, Whiteread became the first woman to win the Turner Prize, an accolade presented annually to a British visual artist; previous victors include Damien Hirst, Gilbert & George, and Anish Kapoor. Four years after her win, in 1997, she was the first woman to represent Britain at the Venice Biennale. Her work primarily focuses on casting, and her Turner Prize-winning exhibit House (1993) featured a life-sized concrete cast of a Victorian terraced house in east London. Whiteread’s work has been exhibited in the Tate Museum, Paris’ Centre Pompidou and New York’s Metropolitan Museum of Art and the Museum of Modern Art. Whiteread’s vision for the 2027 trophy features a steely, silver frame with holes punctuated throughout a silver frame alongside holes. “I used the motif of the BRIT Award and tried to change it in some way,” she said in a statement. “I exposed the interior of the statue – as an artist would do with their music.” Rachel Whiteread Trophy, Studio, London, England, on 16 Nov. 2026. (Photo by 2026 JM Enternational) John Marshall Speaking on the appointment, Glyn Aikins , co-president of RCA Records at Sony Music U.K., called Whiteread one of “Britain’s greatest living artists.” He added, “Rachel has created something that is unmistakably her own and is a fitting tribute to the limitless imagination of the artists we celebrate each year and that also captures what the BRITs stands for in celebrating the very best of British creativity. The artists who lift this trophy will be holding a genuine work of art.” Nominations for the 2027 BRIT Awards will be announced in the coming months. No performers have yet been confirmed.

title: ‘Grand Theft Auto VI’ Soundtrack Drives to No. 1 on ARIA Chart
summary: "GTA" focus track “Flower In A Hurricane” by Justice, Tame Impala, SZA and King Gizzard And The Lizard Wizard roars 17-5 on the national singles chart.
content: There’s no stopping the Grand Theft Auto VI (via Atlantic/Warner) soundtrack, as it motors to No. 1 on the ARIA Albums Chart . Spanning 34 tracks, including songs by Dua Lipa, Justice, Travis Scott, Morgan Wallen and more, GTA is the first soundtrack to top the national albums tally in 2026. Meanwhile, its focus track “Flower In A Hurricane” (Ed Banger/Universal) by Justice, Tame Impala, SZA and King Gizzard And The Lizard Wizard roars 17-5 on the national singles chart, for Tame Impala’s third top 10 this year following “Dracula” and “Loser,” and marking a first-ever appearance in the top 50 for King Gizzard and Justice. Grand Theft Auto VI is the biggest video game drop of the year, or any year , raking in almost $4 billion globally on its first day of release. Following the release of the deluxe version of Daughter From Hell (Interscope/Universal), featuring four new tracks, Gracie Abrams ’ third album bounces 26-6. Daughter From Hell logged one week at No. 1 in late July, for her second leader after 2024’s The Secret Of Us . The all-star Forever Young (Virgin Music Group/Inertia) project from War Child Australia, the domestic arm of the international War Child organization, opens its account at No. 12. The fundraising collection houses songs by Paul Kelly, Missy Higgins, Ruel, Sarah Blasko, The Temper Trap, King Gizz, Grace Cummings, and a new, Paul Mac remix of Youth Group’s cover of Alphaville’s “Forever Young.” It’s the first ever benefit album for War Child Australia, with 100% of proceeds supporting children living through conflict. Other new releases on this week’s albums tally, published Friday, Nov. 27, including Trivium’s Crown In The Grave (at No. 31 via Roadrunner/Warner), the soundtrack to The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping (No. 38 via MCA/Universal), and Down’s Volume V (No. 45 via Nuclear Blast/ADA), while Ninajirachi’s debut LP I Love My Computer (Orchard) returns to the top 40, at No. 40, after the Aussie producer and DJ won best dance/electronic release for “WannaCry” (shared with Porter Robinson) at the 2026 ARIA Awards . Over on the ARIA Singles Chart , Ella Langley ’s “Choosin’ Texas” (Sony) returns to No. 1 for its 17th non-consecutive cycle at the summit. With that result, it’s tied with The Kid Laroi and Justin Bieber’s “Stay” and Alex Warren’s “Ordinary” for the third longest run at the top. Olivia Dean’s “Man I Need” is second with 18 weeks, while the all-time champ is Tones And I’s “Dance Monkey” with 24 total weeks at No. 1. No new debutants impact the latest ARIA Top 50 Singles Chart.

title: Miranda Lambert Heats Up Halftime at Dallas Cowboys’ NFL Thanksgiving Game: Watch
summary: The three-time Grammy Award-winning star delivered a nearly seven-minute medley -- with support from the Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders, a full band and a strings section.
content: Miranda Lambert gave Texans some homestyle country cooking Thursday night (Nov. 26), when she headlined the halftime spot in the NFL Thanksgiving contest between Dallas Cowboys and the visiting Philadelphia Eagles. Wearing a black cowboy hat and a little black dress emblazoned with stars and finished with long, tasseled sleeves, Lambert delivered a nearly seven-minute medley — with support from the Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders, a full band and a strings section. The three-time Grammy Award-winning star kicked things off with “Snakeskin Boots,” and got cooking with “Kerosene,” “Gunpowder & Lead,” “Mama’s Broken Heart,” and a cover of Audra Mae and The Almighty Sound’s “Little Red Wagon.” “Happy Thanksgiving y’all, we love you Texas,” she said at the close. Lambert has been on a tear of late. Just last week, she was the big winner at the 60th annual Country Music Awards, where she collected three trophies. With that hattrick, she lifted her career total of wins to 17, extending her lead as the female artist with the most victories. The Longview, TX native ushered in her new album, Crisco , with a set Oct. 1 at the newly-opened Nashville venue The Truth, then dropped her Songline album on Nov. 13, followed by the companion film Songline on Nov. 20, both via Amazon Music. Also, Lambert co-wrote Ella Langley’ s Billboard Hot 100 smash hit “Choosin’ Texas,” which is now the longest-charting No. 1 in Hot 100 history, with 29 weeks atop the leaderboard. In recent days, “Choosin’ Texas” logged a 50th week atop Billboard ’s Hot Country Songs chart (dated Nov. 28), equaling the all-time mark set by Bebe Rexha and Florida Georgia Line ’s “Meant To Be” in 2017-18. Unfortunately for the home fans at AT&T Stadium in Arlington, TX, Lambert’s halftime spot was the only highlight. The Eagles defeated the Cowboys 39–38, after being down by as much as 21 points in the third-quarter. Eagles kicker Jake Elliott had the dagger, nailing a game-winning field goal with just two seconds on the clock. Watch Lambert’s NFL Thanksgiving halftime performance in full below.

title: Anuel AA’s ‘RHLM2’ Album Is Finally Here: ‘I Made It With My Heart and Soul’
summary: The long-awaited album is a sequel to his 2018 debut, Real Hasta La Muerte, and his first in four years.
content: Anuel AA is celebrating his 34th birthday on Thursday (Nov. 26) with the release of his long-awaited RHLM2 album. Related 5 Things to Know About Anuel AA Ahead of His ‘RHLM2’ Album Release Anuel AA Blames Delayed Bogotá Show on Team Member’s ‘Big Mistake,’ Promises Free Makeup Concert Celebrar y Gratitud: Listen to the Ultimate Thanksgiving Latin Playlist The sequel to his debut studio album, Real Hasta La Muerte (2018), is home to 23 tracks that blend trap and reggaetón. It’s a return to the sound that made him a household name as “El Dios del Trap” (The God of Latin Trap). Though it’s taken the Puerto Rican act nearly 10 years to release the sequel to RHLM — which debuted at No. 1 on Top Latin Albums in July 2018—he has released other promising albums in between, including Emmanuel (2020) and Las Leyendas Nunca Mueren (2021), both of which also hit No. 1 on the chart. “I poured my heart and soul into this album for everyone who believes in me and stays loyal no matter what. This album means the world to me. There are no perfect words to explain how I feel and what I feel for this album,” he said in an Instagram post ahead of the set’s release on Thanksgiving night. He dedicated his new project to his fans, his family and those who have stuck by his side during the good and bad times. He continued: “Thank you for never giving up on me, I love you all so much with all my heart!!!!!!! I made this album for you […] I will never forget you!!!!!” From trapsoul to sensual reggaetón, RHLM2 includes fiery collaborations such as “Sexo Nama” with De La Rose, “Tal Ve Un Ignorante Fui” with ROA and “Si Me Matan a Balazos” with Fuerza Regida. Most notable is “Instagram,” a collaboration with Blessd and Wisin, where they cleverly sample Don Omar’s 2006 hit “Myspace” alongside Wisin y Yandel. The set wraps with five previously released commercial hits—“Amanece” feat. Haze (2018), “Mas Rica Que Ayer” feat. Mambo Kingz & DJ Luian (2022), “¿Qué Nos Pasó?” (2022), “La Llevo al Cielo” feat. Chris Jedi, Chencho Corleone & Ñengo Flow (2022) and the Ovy on the Drums-produced “Deportivo” feat. Blessd (2024)—further reminding fans of his ongoing star power.

title: John Farnham’s Family Gives Rare Update on Legendary Singer’s Health
summary: Farnham continues to stay out of the spotlight after undergoing marathon surgery to remove a cancerous tumor from his throat in 2022.
content: John Farnham ’s spirits remain high, his mind is sharp, but his body is failing. That’s the gist of a rare health update, shared from the legendary Australian singer’s family. These days, the veteran singer is at home but gets around in a wheelchair and requires oxygen. “His mental state is really good,” Rob Farnham, John’s son, told 102.5 ABC Perth Breakfast . “He’s spending a lot of time with his grandson whom he loves. He’s doing a lot of physical therapy. He’s happy, he’s laughing, he’s joking.” John Farnham’s wife is a constant at his side. “Mum definitely sacrifices herself for dad and to help dad and she’s an amazing woman and we’re very proud of her as well,” Rob Farnham explains. “Obviously sometimes she gets a bit down but she has us to lean on and that’s what your family support is.” The revered pop singer continues to stay out of the spotlight after undergoing marathon surgery in 2022 to remove a cancerous tumor from his throat. He will never sing again, his reps confirmed in May, but the time away from the public glare hasn’t dimmed his superstar status in these parts. Farnham was the focus of an all-star concert at Melbourne’s Rod Laver Arena on Sept. 20, featuring 120 artists and musicians, all of them selected by Farnham. The concert, a swift sellout, was cinecast into Hoyt’s theaters and served as a fundraiser for Head and Neck Cancer Australia . He was unable to attend, due to his condition. And when a jukebox musical based on Farnham’s career premiered recently in Sydney , he stayed away, which prompted the health update. With 1986’s Whispering Jack, Farnham orchestrated one of the all-time great comebacks. The album spent 25 weeks at No. 1 in Australia, en route to shifting more than one million copies, becoming the first domestic LP to do so. It remains the highest-selling album ever in Australia by a local talent. Whispering Jack, of course, features Farnham’s signature song, “You’re The Voice,” a top 10 hit in the United Kingdom, and, four decades on, the unofficial anthem of Australia. He was named Australian of the Year in 1987, was named Officer of the Order of Australia in 1996, was inducted into the ARIA Hall of Fame in 2003 and has collected 19 career ARIA Awards.

title: ‘True Family’: Nile Rodgers Remembers Duran Duran’s Andy Taylor
summary: "RIP my dear friend. We were always happy when we were together. I love you," Rodgers writes.
content: You can’t choose you family. But you can choose your true family . That’s how Nile Rodgers remembers Andy Taylor , the founding guitarist of Duran Duran and The Power Station, who died this week following a years-long battle with prostate cancer, at the age of 65 . Rodgers, like millions of music fans around the globe, is mourning the Englishman’s passing. “Dear Andy Taylor RIP. How many countless great days and nights did we have?,” he writes. “I was sleeping last night when I heard the news of your passing. #RIP my dear friend. We were always happy when we were together. I love you.” Rodgers and Taylor go way back. The Chic mainstay and elite record producer worked with Duran Duran on many of their hits, a friendship that began with the British new wave legends’ first U.S. No. 1 “The Reflex” from 1984. Chic’s bass player Bernard Edwards produced the 1985 debut album from The Power Station, which gathered Duran Duran’s Andy and John Taylor, along with English singer Robert Palmer and U.S. drummer Tony Thompson. Rodgers provided some informal assistance to the project, which yielded the hits “Some Like It Hot” and a cover of Marc Bolan’s “Get It On (Bang A Gong)”. “ #BernardEdwardsRIP loved you, and #TonyThompsonRIP loved you,” adds Rodgers, a cancer survivor. “Our two bands will be forever linked in the most special way. True family. Peace and eternal love.” Rodgers shared a happy snap of himself with Andy, from somewhere, sometime in the 1980s, slapped with the caption: “The way I’ll always think of us…guitarist brothers.” It’s been a heartbreaking month for Duranies. Earlier, the band’s founding drummer Roger Taylor announced he was hanging up his sticks due to worsening tinnitus . Andy Taylor (no relation with John and Roger) had multiple stints in Duran Duran, scoring 13 hits on the Billboard Hot 100 , including No. 1s with “The Reflex” and “A View to a Kill” in 1985. The group’s beloved second album Rio album (which housed “Hungry Like the Wolf,” “Save a Prayer,” “My Own Way,” and the title track) hit the Billboard 200 in 1982 and remained on the chart for a whopping 128 weeks. He had two stints with Duran Duran, including their all-conquering run through the first half of the ’80s, during which he gave true grit to the band’s sound, both with his guitar and rockstar swagger. Taylor was inducted into the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame in 2022 in absentia due to his illness, which his bandmates revealed for the very first during their induction speech. title: Live Nation Adds Venue on Australia’s Gold Coast
summary: Surfers Music Hall will be a 2,500-capacity live music space in Surfers Paradise, with a target to open its doors in mid-2028.
content: GOLD COAST, Australia — Live Nation continues to expand its venues portfolio in Australia, adding a new facility on the Gold Coast. Announced this week, Surfers Music Hall will be a 2,500-capacity live music space in Surfers Paradise, the hometown of chart-topping pop star Amy Shark , with a target to open its doors in mid-2028. Surfers Music Hall will be the concerts giant’s first venue on the Gold Coast, and the first dedicated live music venue of this scale in the region. When complete, the space will bring more national and international tours to the Gold Coast, the second biggest city in Queensland, “while giving local artists a new stage,” reads a statement. Bookings will be open “to a range of promoters,” the message continues. The timing of the new venue is critical. Queensland’s music and entertainment communities are preparing for the opportunity of a lifetime, when Brisbane hosts the 2032 Summer Olympic Games and Paralympic Games. The Gold Coast, about 50 miles south of Brisbane, won’t miss out. Hockey, triathlon, marathon swimming, and basketball games are earmarked for the city. The buzz is building for the local music scene, too, which has hosted concerts from the likes of Pearl Jam, Foo Fighters and Queen at Carrara Stadium. Also, Live Nation and the City of Gold Coast hosted a Ones to Watch showcase in 2022, and the 2026 Queensland Music Awards (QMAs) were presented on the Gold Coast for the first time in the event’s 20-year history. Surfers Music Hall will be owned by The City of Gold Coast and operated by Live Nation, and is located within the former Surfers Paradise Transit Centre and Bruce Bishop Carpark precinct. The development, according to LN, is expected to contribute an average of A$20 million ($13 million) each year to the local economy, support some 100 ongoing jobs and create jobs for the creative industries. As previously reported, Live Nation, OVG and Plenary have been green-lit to build the Gather Brisbane arena ahead of the Games, a 17,000-plus capacity facility that will make the Sunshine State’s capital a two-arena town. Currently, LN operates the Fortitude Music Hall (3,000) and The Triffid (800) in Brisbane, and boasts a national network of sites, including The Palais Theatre (2,900 capacity) and Festival Hall in Melbourne; Hindley Street Music Hall in Adelaide (1,800), Anita’s Theatre in Wollongong (1,200); and the 13,000-capacity Spark Arena in Auckland, New Zealand. Earlier , LN announced it would deliver and operate a purpose-built, 5,000 capacity venue at Arden Central in North Melbourne, and its Northbridge Music Hall in Perth is expected to open to the public in the summer of 2026-27. Brisbane won the rights to host the Olympics in 2021 when the IOC declared the city as the “preferred candidate,” thanks to its proven track record for organizing international events, with the Commonwealth Games — two, including the Gold Coast in 2018, an Expo and the Goodwill Games in its good books.
